free_tier.stated: Free tier, quoted: '1 App Replica (0.5 GB memory)', 'Free Tier PostgreSQL Database', 'Custom Domains & SSL', 'Zero-downtime Deploys'. The free database is capped at '10k Rows' and '2 connections'. Paid Standard is 'USD 10/mo' for 0.2 GB, scaling to 'Up to 384 GB' of replica memory and '10+ (Horizontal)' replicas.

retention.stated: a Free app 'Sleeps after 30 days' without a deploy, and the free database stops at 10,000 rows and 2 connections, which a real workload reaches first.

egress.terms: Standard production bandwidth is included with the provisioned resources, with no per-GB price and no numeric allowance published; a fair-use policy applies to extremely high-volume egress, and the page recommends Dedicated Ingress at USD 250/mo for massive data transfer.

record.interface_detail: the gigalixir CLI (macOS, Linux, Windows); SSH and a remote console on every plan; no REST API page was found
record.tooling: the gigalixir CLI installs with a one-line script; SSH and a remote console are available on every plan
record.chaining: an Elixir or Phoenix app plus a 10,000-row Postgres on one free tier is a complete small backend with no charge; the free replica publishes no vCPU number, so sizing it needs a run rather than a table.

record.notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev says 'one free instance that never sleeps and a free-tier PostgreSQL database limited to 2 connections, 10,000 rows'. The 'never sleeps' half is wrong: the vendor table says Free 'Sleeps after 30 days' of no deploy and only Standard never sleeps. The aggregator omits the card requirement at signup, which is the identity cost that decides whether this is reachable. vCPU is not published for the free replica and is null rather than guessed.
